result.summary: Restored the argparse description in `forgel_code/cli.py` to the previous release's exact wording (`Thin console client for Forgel over the engine's machine-readable commands.`) by dropping only the added sentence `Run it without a command to open the interactive session.` Nothing else in the file, the parser, the commands, the fall-through into the interactive session on an empty argv, or the one-shot output/exit-status paths was touched. Added `tests/test_cli_help_description.py`, which pins the released description text in the parser and in `--help` (both in-process and as a real `python -m forgel_code --help` process) and asserts the help output no longer mentions the interactive session; no existing test asserted the removed sentence, so none was weakened or deleted. Verified with `git diff forgel_code/cli.py` (single-line description change), `python -m forgel_code --help` (prints the released description, no interactive sentence), and the full suite `python -m pytest`: 382 passed.

review.summary: The attributed change does exactly what the release audit finding requires: `forgel_code/cli.py` drops the appended sentence "Run it without a command to open the interactive session." from the argparse `description`, leaving "Thin console client for Forgel over the engine's machine-readable commands." — the sentence the audit identified as the sole addition, so removing it restores the previously released wording with no other line in the file (usage text, option help, subcommand help, version output, or one-shot handling) touched. The no-argument path still routes to `run_interactive()`, so the interactive session remains reachable as required, and every other command path is byte-identical because no other code changed. The newly added `tests/test_cli_help_description.py` does not assert the removed sentence (it asserts its absence and pins the restored text, both in-process and through a real `--help` subprocess run), so FR-4 is satisfied and no existing test was deleted or weakened. The change set contains only the description restoration and the accompanying help-assertion test; no temporary, debug or generated artifact was committed. QA reports the environment gate and the full suite as passing, and the two review-only criteria (identical previous-release wording, scoped change set) hold when the diff is read. The only observation, non-blocking, is that the new test also rejects the bare word "interactive" anywhere in the help output, which is slightly stronger than the requirement but consistent with it and does not constrain current product behavior.
